claims.text: Conventionally prepared single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering temperatures above 2300 °C.
Spark plasma sintering can densify ZrB2 at temperatures below 2300 °C.
SPS near 2000 °C can produce single-phase ZrB2.
SPS produces denser ZrB2 with fewer residual pores than conventional sintering above 2300 °C.
Rapid heating and cooling during SPS minimizes grain growth in ZrB2.
Electric-current-assisted heating and applied pressure enhance ZrB2 densification and grain bonding.
Pulsed DC current and pressure enhance atomic diffusion and consolidation in ZrB2.
The enhanced diffusion and consolidation caused by SPS lead to full densification with minimal porosity at a lower temperature than conventional sintering.
Reduced porosity limits liquid-plating-bath infiltration or defect development during extended exposure.
Reduced infiltration or defect development decreases hole formation during prolonged plating-bath exposure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will retain strength better than conventionally sintered ZrB2 during long-duration liquid-plating-bath exposure.
SPS-prepared ZrB2 will resist component failure better than conventionally sintered ZrB2 during long-duration liquid-plating-bath exposure.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 tends to have relatively high residual porosity.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 is susceptible to damage from prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure.
